methodological_rigor.justification: Multi-institutional retrospective study (9 institutions, 849 patients: 635 training, 214 validation cohort). Appropriate statistical methods: one-way ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis for group comparisons, ROC curve analysis, Harrell c-index, AIC for model comparison, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, calibration plots with Hosmer-Lemeshow testing. Multivariate Cox regression with appropriate variable selection (p<0.1 univariate). However, retrospective design with potential selection bias from preoperative therapy exclusions.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort study developing preoperative prognostic model for ICC patients undergoing resection. High clinical relevance: model integrates readily available preoperative data (TBS, CEA, CA19-9) to stratify risk and guide surgical decision-making. Nomogram simple enough for routine clinical use. Supports individualized counseling and treatment planning for aggressive malignancy with limited prognostic tools.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive reporting following REMARK guidelines: patient selection criteria, variable definitions, model development, performance metrics (AUC, C-index, AIC, calibration). Training and validation cohorts clearly separated. However, no statement regarding individual patient data availability or code sharing for model implementation.

novelty_literature.justification: First study integrating TBS + CEA + CA19-9 (TCCA model) into single preoperative prognostic model; prior work combined TBS with single biomarker. Novel contribution: comprehensive approach addressing CA19-9/CEA-negative patients. Model methodology (dichotomization of continuous variables, point scoring) relatively standard but application-specific to ICC is incremental advance.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear motivation for simple, practical prognostic tool. Methods comprehensive with rationale for variable selection. Results systematically presented with appropriate comparisons to TNM staging. Discussion contextualizes findings within broader literature and acknowledges limitations including heterogeneous etiology, potential imaging/biomarker variability, and modest AUC values (0.63-0.70).

key_strengths: Multi-institutional cohort (n=849) with separate training/validation sets strengthens generalizability compared to single-center studies
TCCA model outperforms standard AJCC TNM staging (C-index 0.734 vs 0.599) and other composite scores (TBS-CEA 0.648, TBS-CA19-9 0.660)
Simple, clinically practical tool using routine preoperative data; nomogram provides visual aid for patient counseling and risk stratification
Model maintains discriminatory ability in biomarker-negative subgroups (CEA- and CA19-9-negative), addressing known diagnostic limitation
key_concerns: Retrospective design with selection bias from preoperative therapy exclusions; excludes patients with neoadjuvant therapy, potentially enriching more favorable phenotypes
Geographic limitation (China-based cohorts) with high HBV prevalence; generalizability to Western populations unknown
Modest AUC values (0.63-0.70) indicate incomplete discrimination; room for improvement noted by authors
Dynamic biomarker changes (esp. CA19-9 influenced by biliary obstruction) not captured by single preoperative measurement
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid Tier 3 manuscript with practical clinical value. Multi-institutional validation and clear performance advantage over TNM staging support acceptance. Modest AUC and geographic limitation prevent higher tier.
